Chapter 1 • Introduction

1.1 Roadmaps of the Notes

Four infographics, on the large pages that follow, map the territory covered by these notes. Figure 1.1 gives the whole construction at a glance, with no formulas: a smooth manifold, its tangent, cotangent and tensor spaces at every point, the fields assembled from them, and the three structures that can be chosen on top of these fields, up to the Einstein curvature. The three figures after it are detailed versions of this overview. Figure 1.2 collects the algebra of Chapter 2: sets and maps, the scalars \(\mathbb{R}\), the vector space with its dual and its tensor spaces, and their components in a basis. Figure 1.3 carries the construction through Chapters 3, 4 and 5: a set with a topology becomes a topological and then a smooth manifold, whose tangent, cotangent and tensor spaces at every point are finally assembled into vector, covector and tensor fields. Figure 1.4 adds the remaining layers of structure on top of these fields, following Chapters 6, 7 and 8: a connection, which allows fields to be differentiated and compared between points and gives rise to torsion and curvature; a metric, which measures lengths and angles, allowing to compute geodesics; and finally the volume form and the integral of functions and forms over the manifold.

All four figures share the same layout and are read from top to bottom, each level adding one piece of structure to the previous one, while columns align corresponding objects. Every card names the chapter or section where its concepts are defined, and every symbol carries the colour of the structure that introduces it. The overview can be read at a glance; the three detailed figures are not meant to be: they are a reference to come back to, to locate a definition, recall a notation, or see where a given object fits in the overall construction.
